items.title: Trump will raise Iran, not Ukraine, at planned Shenzhen talks with Xi and Putin
items.summary: A White House statement says Ukraine will not be on the agenda when Trump meets Putin and Xi in Shenzhen next week, but he intends to discuss the Iran war, according to Arab News. Details may change as the meeting nears.
items.why: Great-power bargaining over Iran and Ukraine moves oil prices and sanctions that reach Indian companies.

items.title: US says it shot down two Iranian drones heading for Bahrain
items.summary: The US said it stopped two Iranian drones aimed at Bahrain and denied that an IRGC strike hit a US radar. Reports say Trump held off further strikes on Iran at the request of Gulf allies. Early reporting, so details are provisional.
items.why: Gulf tension keeps crude and shipping costs high, which feeds into Indian inflation and company margins.

items.title: FAA orders a nationwide ground stop over tower communication faults
items.summary: The FAA issued a national ground stop citing communications problems at air traffic control towers, and Homeland Security ruled out a cyberattack, the same report says. Provisional while the cause is confirmed.
items.why: Shows how fragile critical infrastructure is, a recurring theme in risk and operations case discussions.

items.title: China makes trade and green-tech tariffs a priority at COP31
items.summary: Climate Home News reports that China wants COP31 to address unilateral trade measures and the free flow of green technology, while the EU says the process should not become a forum for trade disputes. This preview was published in October, so it shows what to expect, not an outcome.
items.why: Tariff fights over solar, EVs and wind decide where green jobs and supply chains are built.

items.title: EU and UK move to suspend a 10% EV tariff for two years
items.summary: A trade newsletter says the EU and UK plan to suspend for two years a 10% tariff on electric vehicles, which industry warns would leave them open to cheap Chinese models. Described as a plan, not a final decision, so treat it as provisional.
items.why: Trade rules shape which firms hire and expand in the auto and clean-tech sectors.

items.title: COP31 leaders' summit ends with electrification pledges
items.summary: The two-day leaders' segment in Antalya closed on 12 November with more countries endorsing the presidency's 35x35 electrification pledge and new philanthropic money for the Tropical Forest Forever Facility, the World Resources Institute says. There was no single negotiated declaration; talks run to 20 November.
items.why: Electrification targets shape green-skills demand and the sustainability claims brands can make.

items.title: Retail inflation hits 6.09%, above the RBI's ceiling
items.summary: October CPI inflation rose to 6.09% from 5.54% in September, the first breach of the RBI's 6% upper limit in two years and above a Reuters poll forecast of 5.93%. Rural inflation was 6.63% and urban 5.41%.
items.why: Higher prices squeeze household budgets and salary planning, and change how brands price and promote.

items.title: October exports hit a record $89.99 billion
items.summary: Commerce Secretary Rajesh Aggarwal reported October exports of about $89.99 billion, the highest monthly figure on record: $49.47 billion in goods and $40.51 billion in services. The trade deficit narrowed to $20.09 billion. Minister Piyush Goyal said exports could cross $1 trillion this year, up from $863 billion last year.
items.why: Strong exports mean more hiring in logistics, manufacturing and IT services, the firms that recruit from campuses.

items.title: RBI reportedly plans to stop private equity firms controlling several NBFCs
items.summary: A 12 November report says the RBI plans to bar private equity firms from controlling more than one non-bank lender. Reported plan, not yet a final rule.
items.why: Rules on who owns lenders affect consumer-finance brands and the job market in financial services.

items.title: RBI floats a one-hour delay for large UPI transfers
items.summary: The central bank has floated a one-hour delay for UPI transfers above ₹10,000 as a safety measure, according to a report. It is a proposal, so the final rule may differ.
items.why: Any friction in UPI changes how fintech and retail brands design checkout and payments.

items.title: Sensex and Nifty extend a strong November on foreign buying
items.summary: On 12 November the Sensex touched 82,057 and the Nifty traded near 25,342 in early deals, with WTI crude near $85 a barrel. Market experts link the Nifty's 9.55% rise over seven sessions mainly to foreign institutional buying. The report predates 14 November.
items.why: Market sentiment moves campus hiring plans and the equity-linked pay of the firms you will join.

items.title: Qualcomm starts India layoffs, about 1,000 jobs reportedly at risk
items.summary: Qualcomm has begun laying off staff in India as part of a global restructuring, starting with its Bengaluru facility, Business Standard reports. The company has not confirmed numbers; the roughly 1,000 figure and a second wave in January 2027 come from media reports.
items.why: A live case on how multinationals run layoffs, severance and communication, directly relevant to HR practice.

items.title: Tech layoff tracker counts 206,817 people cut in 2026
items.summary: TrueUp's tracker lists 712 tech layoffs affecting 206,817 people so far in 2026, with Qualcomm among the latest entries. Tracker figures are compiled from public reports.
items.why: The scale of cuts shapes how employers talk about reskilling, redeployment and employer brand.

items.title: Trump approves a diesel deal that waives sanctions on Russian fuel
items.summary: Search reports say Trump recently approved a deal waiving sanctions to allow sales of millions of tons of Russian diesel, blaming high energy prices on Ukrainian refinery strikes, though analysts point mainly to the Iran war. Details are early and provisional.
items.why: Fuel prices drive costs across Indian industry and consumer spending.

items.title: OpenAI launches ChatGPT Wallet for agent purchases
items.summary: OpenAI launched ChatGPT Wallet on 13 November, built with American Express, Mastercard and Visa, letting its AI agents make purchases for users. Reported by news aggregators; check OpenAI's own announcement for details.
items.why: Agent-led shopping could change how brands are discovered and how marketing reaches customers.

items.title: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang reported to have resigned; staff urge his return
items.summary: A Fox News live blog reports that Nvidia's chief executive resigned and that some staff want him back, with Colette Kress named interim CEO in other reports. A House committee is also reported to be threatening a subpoena. This is early live-blog reporting, so treat it as provisional.
items.why: Leadership shocks at a company this large test succession planning and investor communication.

items.title: Google Labs opens Tabletop, a shared AI planning experiment
items.summary: Google Labs opened Tabletop, an AI experiment for shared planning spaces, available by waitlist in the US to users 18 and older, according to an AI news digest.
items.why: Collaborative AI tools are changing how teams plan, a skill HR and marketing roles now need.

items.title: US weighs AI chip export licences for seven countries
items.summary: The Trump administration is reportedly considering export licences for controlled AI chips going into data centres in Singapore, Malaysia, Thailand, Indonesia, Norway, Brazil and South Africa, with an announcement possible this month.
items.why: Where AI chips can go decides where data-centre jobs and investment land.

items.title: Budget phone makers turn to recycled memory as costs surge
items.summary: Rising memory prices are pushing low-end smartphone makers towards recycled memory, while Samsung leans on its scale. Counterpoint Research says memory and storage now make up as much as 54% of component costs in ultra-low-end models.
items.why: Component costs decide entry-level phone prices in India, a key mass-market category.

items.title: RBI's inflation band is 2% to 6%
items.summary: The RBI targets 4% inflation with a tolerance band of 2% to 6%; October's 6.09% is the first reading above it since October 2024 (6.21%).
items.why: A number worth knowing for any economy question in an interview.

items.title: Indian benchmarks are up over 10% this month
items.summary: The Nifty 50 and Sensex had delivered more than 10% month to date as of 12 November.
items.why: Context for how strong November has been for markets.

items.title: Global fossil-fuel emissions were broadly flat in 2026
items.summary: UN Secretary-General António Guterres told COP31 that global fossil fuel carbon emissions remained broadly stable in 2026.
items.why: A useful data point for sustainability discussions.
